concurrencyAndPrefix.finding: The existing creating/admission/debug thread is the only callback producer. Scopes calls it after the existing startup.accept result and only for its already captured WOW64 child record. No additional startup decision, exception, read, HANDLE query or ContinueDebugEvent is introduced.

Producer selects its next index by relaxed count load, initializes that complete eight-DWORD slot, then release-stores index+1. Rows below each published count are never reused or mutated. The one consumer acquire-loads count and reads only [0,count). Reading a release-published count makes all earlier row writes visible. A producer writing a later slot outside that prefix does not change the selected bytes.

Output HANDLE configuration occurs while the original broker state lock is still held, before runDebugLoop unlocks it. The original main Release branch acquires that same lock. Handle state is immutable afterward. The distinct Scopes mutex is not falsely used as the broker-state fence for row bytes; atomic count publication supplies that row relation.

Count cannot exceed16. Each row is eight DWORDs/32 bytes, so the selected write is at most512 bytes. Slots0..14 retain ordinary type1 fields; slot15 retains reserved overflow type2 and its original sequence. At cap no later row is published. The same decoder refuses an observed overflow record.

Only the acquired prefix is attested. There is no promise that the load includes every possible later observation or that all debug events have completed. Disabled observer or acquired count0 performs no I/O and returns true; enabled empty trace still fails the unchanged TS observation assertion. An omitted future overflow or later row is not proved absent by this prefix.

releaseAndErrorOrder.finding: Original state acquisition, confirmed absence, no Stop busy, original Job CloseHandle and releaseAccepted assignment precede the new hook. The hook precedes construction/enqueueing of Released. One ordinary Release exits the command loop; there is no added read or repeat flush. Existing refused Release requests before those prerequisites remain refused.

The one synchronous WriteFile must return true AND written==requested. A false result or short count takes existing abandon(wire::WriteFailure) before any Released success is enqueued. No retry, secondary write or new record/protocol is added. This closes the old row-aligned short-prefix acceptance gap for the requested prefix, without asserting whole-trace completeness or fsync.

Both successful ExitProcess paths require the complete Released ACK and original terminal success selection. Those cannot precede this main-thread flush and reply enqueue. abandon takes no state/reply mutex, seals and invokes unchanged first-failure termination. Existing first failure wins; otherwise new WriteFailure73 may become first. A failed/short write is a native TEST failure even if some bytes were written. The existing callback code==0 assertion and guarded first-error retention remain unchanged.

Original target/Job absence checks and original Job closure precede the TEST write. No new custody signal or process authority is acquired. Removing the old after-debug-loop flush means a refusal before accepted Release may leave buffered observations unpersisted. No failure-path flush is added; this loss of best-effort failure output is explicit in the incoming R1.

The bounded byte count does not establish bounded write latency. New synchronous write and atomic operations consume the existing external scenario/controller budget; they have no free-cost or startup-performance guarantee. The writer ACK deadline is created in the original writer path after dequeue, so it is not a newly proved timeout around the preceding synchronous file write. No timeout constant or native command is changed.
